x: The Western Ghats were inscribed as a natural World Heritage Site in 2012 and span six States, not seven, so D is the wrong pair. Great Himalayan NP (Himachal Pradesh, 2014), Kaziranga (Assam, 1985) and Sundarbans (West Bengal, 1987) are correctly matched.

The Krishna meets the Tungabhadra at Sangameswaram (Nandyal). The Konaseema delta with seven distributaries belongs to the Godavari, Hamsaladeevi is the Krishna's sea outlet (the Godavari reaches the sea at Antarvedi), and the Krishna's course in AP is about 485 km, not 536 km.

The Sabari joins the Godavari near Kunavaram in Andhra Pradesh. Sangameswaram is where the Tungabhadra (not the Indravati) joins the Krishna, and the Pranhita joins the Godavari near Kaleshwaram, not Nizamabad.

About 250 km of the Godavari's 1,465 km lies in Andhra Pradesh. Only about 885 km of the Brahmaputra lies in India (not 250 km); 1,465 km is the Godavari's length (the Kaveri is 805 km), and 2,525 km is the Ganga's (the Mahanadi is 858 km).

The Arabian Sea branch strikes the Western Ghats first, giving very heavy rain at Agumbe and Hulikal on the Ghats crest. It is this branch (not the Bay branch) that moves north along the west coast and leaves a rain shadow east of the Ghats, while the Bay of Bengal branch (not the Arabian Sea branch) strikes the Meghalaya hills.
